subject: Bespoke retention & deletion windows — Q&A and order form next steps
messages:
From: Frank Huang <frank@zephyrbio.com>
To: camila_reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Bespoke retention windows and deletion timelines — initial questions

Hi Camila,

Thanks for the product overview last week. We're getting ready to finalize our procurement and have two specific asks around the Order Form / SLA:

1) Data residency: We need confirmation that customer data and backups for the Zephyr account will persist only in us-west-2 (no cross-region replication).
2) Retention & deletion: We run regulated studies and need a bespoke deletion timeline where primary data is retained for 24 months, but all backups and logs are destroyed within 30 days of deletion request.

Can Redwood support this as part of the Order Form, and if so, what will that look like in terms of timelines and verification (audit logs / attestations)? Procurement is aiming to sign by Nov 14.

Appreciate a quick confirm and any draft language we can feed into our legal team.

Best,
Frank Huang\Director of IT Security\Zephyr Biotech

--
Frank Huang
Frank.Huang@zephyrbio.com

From: camila_reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>

Cc: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Bespoke retention windows and deletion timelines — initial questions

Frank — thanks, and great to hear procurement has a target date. Quick answers up front:

- Residency: yes, we can restrict primary storage and backups to us-west-2 for a private account; we'll add a clause to the Order Form to prohibit cross-region replication without written consent.
- Retention/deletion: we can offer a bespoke schedule: primary data retained 24 months; when a deletion request is submitted we will purge primary copies within 48 hours and enforce deletion of backups and logs within 30 calendar days.

I've attached a first-pass Order Form draft and an SLA_retention_schedule spreadsheet that maps the timelines and the technical actions (purge, overwrite, KMS key rotation, backup retention). See attachments: Zephyr_OrderForm_draft_v1.pdf, SLA_retention_schedule.xlsx.

Looping in Aditya from legal to confirm contract language and Marissa for the engineering confirmation on backups/logs and KMS behavior.

Next steps: if legal/engineering are aligned we'll convert the draft to an amendment and provide a DocuSign-ready version.

Cheers,
Camila Reyes\Account Executive — Strategic Customers\Redwood Inference\camila_reyes@redwood.com\Tel: +1 (415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: Bespoke retention windows and deletion timelines — draft language

Thanks Camila / Frank — I reviewed the draft. A few legal points to make explicit in the Order Form amendment:

1) Definition of "delete": we should specify that "deletion" means irrecoverable removal from live systems and backups such that data recovery is not possible except as required by our internal forensic retention (see item 3).
2) Backups & replication: Redwood will not create cross-region backups unless explicitly authorized; any automatic snapshot used for DR will be retained in us-west-2 only.
3) Forensic/log retention exception: we need to preserve immutable audit logs and security telemetry for a narrow, defined forensic window (not longer than 90 days) unless otherwise compelled by law. We can limit customer-visible backups to 30 days post-deletion request but retain hashed indices/records for 90 days for incident response.

Suggested contract clause (proposal):
"Customer may request deletion of Customer Data. Upon written request, Redwood will: (i) purge Customer Data from active storage within 48 hours; (ii) delete Customer Data from backups within 30 calendar days; and (iii) retain minimal immutable forensic hashes and audit telemetry for up to 90 days solely for security incident investigation, subject to customer-approved access restrictions. Redwood will provide an attestation of deletion within 7 calendar days of completion."

Marissa, please confirm that the 48h / 30d operational targets are feasible and whether the 90-day forensic hashes approach is compatible with our KMS key handling and backup rotation.

- Aditya

Aditya Rao\Senior Counsel, Commercial\Redwood Inference\aditya_rao@redwood.com

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 3 Nov 2025 15:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Bespoke retention windows and deletion timelines — engineering check

On Mon, Nov 3, 2025 at 12:18 PM aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com> wrote:
> Marissa, please confirm that the 48h / 30d operational targets are feasible and whether the 90-day forensic hashes approach is compatible with our KMS key handling and backup rotation.

Quick technical confirm:
- 48h purge of active storage: yes — we can schedule immediate purge jobs and invalidate KV caches within that window.
- 30d backup deletion: feasible for account-scoped backups retained only in us-west-2; we have a controlled rotation policy and will mark snapshots for expedited deletion on the requested timeline.
- Forensic hashes & telemetry (90 days): feasible if we store only salted/hashed indices and not plaintext PII. KMS: we will rotate but retain a limited audit record tied to a deliberately restricted key envelope; customer cannot reconstruct raw data from the hashes.

Operational note: expedited backup deletion will be performed during a maintenance window; we will do our best to complete within 30 days but include a clause that force majeure or court orders may delay timelines.

I'll prepare a short operations appendix for the Order Form that spells out the maintenance window, verification steps, and the deletion attestation artifact format.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole\Director, Platform Reliability\Redwood Inference\marissa_cole@redwood.com
